spreadsheet.title: Spreadsheets
spreadsheet.description: Copy formulas, calculate with SUM, MAX and IF, simulate growth, check formulas and turn European data into suitable charts.

prompts.percentFormula: In C{{row}}, increase the price from B{{row}} by {{value}}%. The rate is in {{address}}. Which formula can be copied down correctly?
prompts.feeFormula: Add a fixed fee of €{{value}} to every value in column B. It is stored in {{address}}. Which formula can be copied down correctly?
prompts.linearGrowth: The quantity grows by the same amount each year ({{step}} here). Which formula belongs in B3 and can be copied down?
prompts.exponentialGrowth: The quantity grows by the same percentage each year ({{step}}% here). Which formula belongs in B3 and can be copied down?
prompts.temperatureChart: Which chart best shows how the temperature in {{city}} changes over the year?
prompts.rainfallChart: Which chart best compares annual rainfall in these European cities?
prompts.conditionShipping: From the order value in F1 on, shipping is free; otherwise €{{fee}} is added. What does {{address}} show?
prompts.checkPercent: Every price in column C should rise by the percentage in F1. The formula was copied down from C2. Is it right in C{{row}}?
prompts.functionGoal: {{cell}} should show $t(games.spreadsheet.goals.{{series}}.{{goal}}). Which formula goes there?
prompts.checkGoal: {{cell}} should show $t(games.spreadsheet.goals.{{series}}.{{goal}}). Is the formula in {{cell}} right?
prompts.functionReverse: {{cell}} shows {{value}}. Which formula calculated this value?
prompts.cellCount: How many cells does =SUMME({{range}}) add up?
prompts.conditionColumn: Column C shows “{{then}}” or “{{otherwise}}”, depending on the value in F1. Which formula was in C2 before it was copied down?
prompts.conditionCount: The formula from C2 was copied down to C6. How many times does column C show “{{then}}”?
prompts.conditionDiscount: From the order value in F1 on, there is a €{{amount}} discount. What does {{address}} show?
prompts.conditionComparison: Which condition is TRUE (WAHR) exactly when the value in B2 is $t(games.spreadsheet.comparisons.{{comparison}}) the value in F1?
prompts.currencyFormula: Column C should convert the prices from column B into {{currency}}. The rate (€1 = {{rate}} {{currency}}) is in {{address}}. Which formula can be copied down correctly?
prompts.afterCopy: The formula in {{from}} is copied to {{to}}. Which formula is in {{to}} then?
prompts.mixedFormula: B2 should show the price from column A times the quantity from row 1. Which formula can be copied right and down and fills the whole table correctly?
prompts.shareFormula: Column C should show each row's share of the total in B7. Which formula belongs in C2 and can be copied down?
prompts.growthFormula: $t(games.spreadsheet.growthContexts.{{context}}) Which formula belongs in B3 and can be copied down?
prompts.growthModel: How do the values in column B change?
prompts.growthNext: The formula in B3 was copied down. Which value appears in {{cell}}?
prompts.growthParameter: The formula in B3 was copied down. Which value is in E1?
prompts.plantChart: Which chart best shows how the sunflower grows week by week?
prompts.batteryChart: Which chart best shows how the phone battery drains over the day?
prompts.julyRainChart: Which chart best compares the July rainfall of these cities?
prompts.populationChart: Which chart best compares the populations of these capitals and big cities?
prompts.kioskChart: Which chart best compares the sales at the school kiosk?
prompts.commuteChart: A survey shows how the class gets to school. Which chart best shows the parts of the whole?
prompts.pocketMoneyChart: What is pocket money spent on? Which chart best shows what part of the whole each item makes up?
prompts.iceChart: Do ice-cream sales at the kiosk depend on the temperature? Which chart shows this best?
prompts.sunshineChart: Are sunnier cities also warmer in July? Which chart shows the relationship best?
prompts.checkFee: Every price in column C should get the fee from F1 added. The formula was copied down from C2. Is it right in C{{row}}?
prompts.checkCurrency: Column C should show the prices in {{currency}}; the rate is in F1. The formula was copied down from C2. Is it right in C{{row}}?
prompts.checkShare: Column C should show each row's share of the total in B7. The formula was copied down from C2. Is it right in C{{row}}?
prompts.checkRule: Column C should show “{{then}}” when the value in B is $t(games.spreadsheet.comparisons.{{comparison}}) the value in F1. The formula was copied down from C2. Is it right in C{{row}}?

examples.chart: A line makes change over time visible.
examples.range: B2:B6 means every cell from B2 to B6.
examples.condition: WENN(condition; then; else), WENN means IF
examples.check: A semicolon instead of a colon: only B2 and B6 count.

references.name: Cell References When Copying
references.summary: Use relative and absolute cell references correctly
references.rules: In {{questionsPerRound}} tasks, choose the formula that can be copied without errors, or predict what a cell contains after copying. Relative references move along; $ fixes a column or row. You have {{duration}} seconds.

growth.name: Simulating Growth
growth.rules: In {{questionsPerRound}} tasks, choose the matching formula, recognise the growth model, continue the simulation or read the parameter in E1. A fixed increase or a fixed percentage? You have {{duration}} seconds.

charts.name: The Right Chart
charts.summary: Visualise European and everyday data appropriately
charts.rules: For {{questionsPerRound}} data sets, choose the chart that answers the question most clearly: change over time, comparison, parts of a whole or relationship. You have {{duration}} seconds.

functions.name: SUMME, MAX, MIN and MITTELWERT
functions.summary: SUMME, MAX, MIN and MITTELWERT over a range
functions.rules: For {{questionsPerRound}} sheets, read what a function calculates, find the right formula or count the cells in a range. Watch the range: B2:B6 covers every cell from B2 to B6, B2;B6 only two. You have {{duration}} seconds.

conditions.name: The WENN (IF) Function
conditions.summary: Use WENN (IF) to show different results depending on a condition
conditions.rules: In {{questionsPerRound}} tasks, evaluate WENN (IF) formulas, count their results or find the right formula and condition. Watch > and >= when a value sits exactly on the limit. You have {{duration}} seconds.

check.name: Checking Formulas
check.summary: Find mistakes in formulas: range, function or reference
check.rules: Check {{questionsPerRound}} formulas to see whether they solve the task. If not: is the range wrong, is it the wrong function, or is a $ sign missing? You have {{duration}} seconds.

laps.min: the fewest laps run by one class

example.title: Example Game
example.description: A one-stage example game to test the framework.

tap.name: Tap Race
tap.summary: Click as often as you can
tap.rules: Click as many times as possible in {{duration}} seconds. Target: {{targetScore}} clicks!

squareroot.title: Square Root Challenge
squareroot.description: Square roots as a speed round, on the number line and by category.
squareroot.clickOnLine: Click on the number line to estimate the value
squareroot.simplifyHint: Leave the factor empty for 1, and the radicand empty for a whole number. Pull every square out of the root.
squareroot.bisectPrompt: Is √{{value}} smaller or larger than {{mid}}? Pick the half it lies in.
squareroot.bisectDone: The interval is narrow enough ({{target}}). Submit it!

speed.name: Speed Round
speed.summary: Solve perfect square roots as fast as possible
speed.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} square roots as fast as possible. All answers are natural numbers. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

numberline.name: Number Line
numberline.summary: Estimate irrational roots on the number line
numberline.rules: Estimate {{questionsPerRound}} square roots by clicking on the number line. The closer you are to the real value, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

classify.name: Classify
classify.rules: Classify {{questionsPerRound}} square roots as natural, rational or irrational. Each correct answer is worth 100 points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

simplify.name: Root Laws
simplify.summary: Write roots as simply as possible
simplify.rules: Simplify {{questionsPerRound}} root terms — no calculator. Pull every square out of the root: √72 becomes 6√2. You have {{duration}} seconds.

bisect.name: Interval Halving
bisect.summary: Trap an irrational root step by step
bisect.rules: Trap {{questionsPerRound}} roots between two numbers. Halve the interval again and again and always keep the root inside — the fewer halvings, the more points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

analysis.title: Analysis Challenge
analysis.description: Calculus: pick the derivative, draw the graph, draw the derivative.
analysis.pointsHint: Work out the y-intercept and the turning points first, then drag the {{count}} points there — the curve follows them.
analysis.pointsExtraHint_one: Tap the grid for one more point, tap a point to take it away again.
analysis.pointsExtraHint_other: Tap the grid for up to {{count}} more points, tap a point to take it away again.

multiple-choice.name: Pick the Derivative
multiple-choice.rules: Pick the correct derivative f'(x) from 4 options for {{questionsPerRound}} functions. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

draw-graph.name: Draw the Graph
draw-graph.summary: Sketch f(x) on the coordinate grid
draw-graph.rules: Draw the graph of {{questionsPerRound}} functions on the coordinate grid. The more accurate your drawing, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

draw-derivative.name: Draw the Derivative
draw-derivative.summary: Sketch f'(x) from the graph of f(x)
draw-derivative.rules: Draw the derivative f'(x) for {{questionsPerRound}} given functions. The dashed curve shows f(x). You have {{duration}} seconds.

rational.title: Rational Numbers
rational.description: Place rational numbers on the number line and calculate with them.
rational.arrangePrompt: Pick a number, then click on the number line
rational.arrangePromptSelected: Click on the number line to place the selected number
rational.arrangePromptAdjust: Drag the marks to place them more exactly
rational.orderPromptAsc: Tap the numbers one after another — smallest first
rational.orderPromptDesc: Tap the numbers one after another — largest first

answerHint.fraction: Leave the denominator empty for a whole number. Equivalent fractions count as correct.
answerHint.decimal: Enter the result as a decimal, e.g. 0.75.
answerHint.both: Enter the result as a fraction (3/4) or as a decimal (0.75).

rational.signPrompt: Is the result positive or negative?
rational.changeAskResult: Click on the number line where you end up.
rational.changeAskChange: Which change leads from the start to the end state?

arrange.name: Arrange on the Number Line
arrange.summary: Place fractions and decimals at the right spot
arrange.rules: Place {{questionsPerRound}} sets of rational numbers on the number line. The closer each number sits to its real position, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

order.name: Put in Order
order.summary: Tap rational numbers and absolute values in order of size
order.rules: Put {{questionsPerRound}} sets of numbers in order of size — tap them one after another in the order asked for. An absolute value like |−3| counts for what it is worth. The more numbers that stand the right way round, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

calculate.name: Calculate
calculate.summary: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions
calculate.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} calculations with rational numbers and enter the result. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

signs.name: Sign Duel
signs.summary: Work out terms with positive and negative numbers
signs.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} terms with positive and negative numbers — no calculator. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

change.name: Changes
change.summary: Follow a change on the number line
change.rules: Follow {{questionsPerRound}} changes: place the end state on the number line, or name the change that leads there. You have {{duration}} seconds.

chance.title: Chance
chance.description: Work out probabilities and fill in tree diagrams.

laplaceHint.fraction: Favourable outcomes over possible outcomes. Equivalent fractions count as correct.
laplaceHint.decimal: Enter the probability as a decimal, e.g. 0.25.
laplaceHint.percent: Enter the probability in percent, e.g. 25.

chance.treePrompt: Drag the probabilities onto the second-stage branches — or tap a card and then a branch.
chance.treeIncomplete: Every branch of the second stage needs a probability.

setups.cards: One card is drawn from a deck of 32 cards.
setups.urn: An urn holds {{red}} red and {{blue}} blue balls. You draw one ball.
setups.wheel: A wheel of fortune has {{sectors}} equal sectors, {{winning}} of them win.
setups.urnTwiceWith: An urn holds {{red}} red and {{blue}} blue balls. You draw one ball, put it back, and draw again.
setups.urnTwiceWithout: An urn holds {{red}} red and {{blue}} blue balls. You draw two balls without putting the first one back.
setups.wheelTwice: A wheel of fortune has {{sectors}} equal sectors, {{winning}} of them win. You spin it twice.

laplace.name: Laplace Sprint
laplace.rules: Work out {{questionsPerRound}} probabilities: favourable outcomes over possible outcomes. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

tree.name: Tree Diagram
tree.summary: Fill in a two-stage tree and use the path rules
tree.rules: Complete {{questionsPerRound}} tree diagrams: place the probabilities on the branches of the second stage, then work out the probability of the event. Multiply along a path, add the paths. You have {{duration}} seconds.

extremum.title: Extreme Values
extremum.description: Differentiate without a calculator and solve extreme value problems.
extremum.deriveUnreadable: That cannot be read as a polynomial yet.
extremum.quantityPrompt: What is to become as large as possible here?
extremum.modelPrompt: Drag the right card into the step that is missing.
extremum.optimizePrompt: Now move x until the quantity is as large as possible.

contexts.fence: A rectangular pasture lies along a straight river. {{length}} m of fence are available for the three sides that are not the river. How wide does it have to be to get the largest area?
contexts.garden: A rectangular garden is to be fenced in. {{fence}} m of fence are available for all four sides. How wide does it have to be to get the largest area?
contexts.box: An open box is folded from a square sheet with side {{side}} cm by cutting squares of side x out of the corners. Which x gives the largest volume?
contexts.cuboid: An open box is folded from a sheet {{length}} cm by {{width}} cm by cutting squares of side x out of the corners. Which x gives the largest volume?
contexts.parabola: A rectangle stands on the x-axis with its upper corners on the parabola y = {{height}} - x². Which x gives the largest area?
contexts.triangle: A right triangle has legs of {{width}} cm and {{height}} cm. A rectangle sits in the right angle with its opposite corner on the hypotenuse. Which width x gives the largest area?
contexts.numbers: Two numbers add up to {{sum}}. The first one is x. Which x makes their product largest?
contexts.ticket: A ticket for the school concert costs {{price}} €, and {{visitors}} people come. For every euro the ticket gets cheaper, {{perEuro}} more people come. By how many euros (x) should the price be cut to take the most money?

derive.name: Derivative Sprint
derive.rules: Differentiate {{questionsPerRound}} polynomials — no calculator, as in the written exam. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

optimize.name: Extreme Value Problem
optimize.summary: From the model to the maximum — one step at a time or all of it
optimize.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} extreme value problems. Sometimes only one step is missing — the quantity, the quantity in two variables, the constraint or the target function — and sometimes the whole way; the rest is already there. Then find the x that makes the quantity largest. Half the points come from the model, half from the maximum. You have {{duration}} seconds.

terme.title: Terms
terme.description: Build, collect, expand and factorise algebraic terms.

prompts.collect: Collect the term as far as you can.
prompts.expand: Remove the brackets and collect like terms.
prompts.factor: Factor out as much as you can.
prompts.binomialFactor: Use a binomial formula to write the term as a product.
prompts.zero: A product is zero exactly when one of its factors is zero.
prompts.zeroFactor: Factorise first — then the zero product rule applies.
prompts.domain: Which number has to be excluded?
prompts.rearrange: Solve the formula for the quantity asked for.
prompts.inequality: Solve the inequality and state the solution.
prompts.value: Work out the value of the term.

hints.expand: Multiply out first, then collect like terms.
hints.factor: The common factor has to come out in full: 12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3), not 2(6x + 9).
hints.binomialExpand: Write the result as a sum, without brackets.
hints.binomialFactor: Write the result as a product, for example (x + 3)² or (x + 4)(x - 4).
hints.zero: Give both solutions, for example 3 and -5. The order does not matter.
hints.fraction: Cross-multiply, or multiply by the denominator. Fractions such as 3/2 are allowed.
hints.domain: The denominator must not become zero. Give the value the variable may not take.
hints.rearrange: Enter the right-hand side only. Any equivalent form counts: U/2 − b and (U − 2b)/2 are both right.
hints.inequality: Write the whole solution, for example x < 4. Type <= for ≤ and >= for ≥. Remember: multiplying or dividing by a negative number turns the relation round.
hints.value: Brackets first, then powers, then multiplication before addition. Fractions such as 5/9 are allowed.
hints.equivalent: Equivalent means: every substitution gives the same value. A single counterexample is enough to disprove it.

contexts.taxi: A taxi charges a base fare of {{a}} € plus {{b}} € for every kilometre driven.
contexts.saving: Mia has saved {{a}} € and adds {{b}} € every week.
contexts.cinema: A cinema ticket costs {{a}} € and a bag of popcorn {{b}} €. Everyone gets both.
contexts.fence: {{a}} m of fence are left over. They mark out a rectangular bed in the corner of a house, with two house walls forming the other sides.
contexts.rectangle: A rectangle is x cm long. It is {{a}} cm narrower than it is long.
contexts.age: Lena is {{a}} years older than Tom.
contexts.pool: A tank holds {{a}} litres of water. {{b}} litres drain off every minute.
contexts.workshop: A workshop charges {{a}} € for the call-out plus {{b}} € for every half hour started.

variables.taxi: x = kilometres driven. Wanted: the price in €.
variables.saving: x = number of weeks. Wanted: Mia's savings in €.
variables.cinema: x = number of people. Wanted: the total price in €.
variables.fence: x = one side of the bed in m. Wanted: its area in m².
variables.rectangle: x = the length in cm. Wanted: the perimeter in cm.
variables.age: x = Tom's age in years. Wanted: their combined age.
variables.pool: x = number of minutes. Wanted: the amount of water in litres.
variables.workshop: x = duration in hours. Wanted: the total on the bill in €.

build.name: Building terms
build.summary: Find the term that matches a situation
build.rules: Read {{questionsPerRound}} situations and pick the term that fits each one. You have {{duration}} seconds.

collect.name: Collecting terms
collect.summary: Add, subtract and multiply like terms
collect.rules: Collect {{questionsPerRound}} terms as far as you can and type the result. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

expand.name: Removing brackets
expand.summary: Expand — including a minus in front of the bracket
expand.rules: Remove the brackets in {{questionsPerRound}} terms and collect like terms. Watch the sign in front of the bracket. You have {{duration}} seconds.

factor.name: Factoring out
factor.rules: Factor the greatest common factor out of {{questionsPerRound}} terms. Only a complete factorisation counts: 12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3). You have {{duration}} seconds.

binomial.name: Binomial formulas
binomial.summary: Use the three formulas in both directions
binomial.rules: Work through {{questionsPerRound}} tasks on the binomial formulas — expanding some, writing others as a product. You have {{duration}} seconds.

zero.name: Zero product rule
zero.summary: Solve equations of the form product = 0
zero.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} equations with the zero product rule: a product is zero exactly when one of its factors is. Give both solutions. You have {{duration}} seconds.

fraction.name: Fractional equations
fraction.summary: Solve ratio and fractional equations, find the domain
fraction.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} equations with fractions. When the variable sits in a denominator you are sometimes asked for the value that has to be excluded. You have {{duration}} seconds.

rearrange.name: Rearranging formulas
rearrange.summary: Solve a formula for one of its other quantities
rearrange.rules: Rearrange {{questionsPerRound}} formulas for the quantity asked for and enter the right-hand side. Any equivalent form counts as correct. You have {{duration}} seconds.

inequality.name: Inequalities
inequality.summary: Solve inequalities — and know when the relation turns round
inequality.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} inequalities and state the solution, for example x < 4. Careful: multiplying or dividing by a negative number turns the relation round. You have {{duration}} seconds.

evaluate.name: Working out terms
evaluate.summary: Substitute values, and check whether two terms are equivalent
evaluate.rules: Work through {{questionsPerRound}} tasks: put numbers into a term and work out its value — or decide whether two terms are equivalent. Mind the order of operations: brackets first, then powers, then multiplication before addition. You have {{duration}} seconds.

python.title: Python Trail
python.description: Read programs, predict their output and hunt down the broken line.

ask.value: What is the value of {{name}} at the end?
ask.count: How often does the innermost statement run?

python.answerSeveral: Every line printed, separated by spaces
python.answerHint_other: The program prints {{count}} lines — write them in the right order.
python.turtlePrompt: Which picture does this program draw?
python.bugsPrompt: Tap the line that holds the mistake.

bugs.colon: A condition or a loop header needs a colon at the end.
bugs.indent: Whatever belongs to the loop has to be indented.
bugs.case: Python is case sensitive — the command is print.
bugs.boolean: The truth values are True and False, capitalised and without quotes.
bugs.quotes: Text needs quotes, or Python goes looking for a variable.
bugs.compare: A condition compares with ==; a single = assigns.
bugs.name: A variable name cannot contain a space.
bugs.call: The arguments of a call belong inside brackets.
bugs.concat: Text and number cannot be joined with + — the number needs str().
bugs.undefined: The variable is used before it has been given a value.
bugs.endless: The counter moves away from the condition — the loop never ends.
bugs.index: Counting starts at 0: the last valid index is len(list) - 1.
bugs.range: The loop runs one step too far and reaches past the list.
bugs.order: A function has to be defined before it is called.

purpose.guess: Let a secret number be guessed and say whether the guess was right.
purpose.sum: Add up every number in a list and print the total.
purpose.square: Draw a square using a function of its own.
purpose.countdown: Count up from 1 to a limit, then print "fertig".
purpose.age: Given an age, say whether it is of full legal age.
purpose.dots: Draw a row of evenly spaced dots.
purpose.max: Find the largest element of a list and print it.
purpose.count: Count how many values of a list are above a limit.

output.name: What comes out?
output.rules: Predict the output of {{questionsPerRound}} short programs. Watch out for /, // and %. The calculator at the bottom is yours to use — the question is what Python works out, not how good your mental arithmetic is. You have {{duration}} seconds.

variables.name: Follow the variable
variables.summary: What is in the variable at the end?
variables.rules: Follow what lands in the variables of {{questionsPerRound}} programs. Every assignment overwrites the old value. You have {{duration}} seconds.

loops.name: Loops
loops.summary: Count the runs, predict the output
loops.rules: Read {{questionsPerRound}} loops: sometimes you count the runs, sometimes you write down every value printed. You have {{duration}} seconds.

branch.name: Branches
branch.rules: Decide for {{questionsPerRound}} programs which line is printed. Python checks from top to bottom and takes the first branch that fits. You have {{duration}} seconds.

logic.name: Logic duel
logic.summary: True or False — and, or and not against the clock
logic.rules: Decide for {{questionsPerRound}} expressions whether they are True or False. Remember what binds first: not before and before or. The faster you are right, the more points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

functions.name: Functions
functions.rules: Predict what the call prints in {{questionsPerRound}} programs. Watch the order of the arguments — and whether the function returns anything at all. You have {{duration}} seconds.

lists.name: Lists
lists.summary: Index, len and the for-in loop
lists.rules: Answer {{questionsPerRound}} questions about lists. Remember: counting starts at 0. You have {{duration}} seconds.

turtle.name: Turtle pictures
turtle.summary: Match the program to its drawing
turtle.rules: Match {{questionsPerRound}} programs to the picture they draw. Watch the number of runs and the angles. You have {{duration}} seconds.

parsons.name: Sort the lines
parsons.summary: Rebuild a program from its shuffled lines
parsons.rules: Put the lines of {{questionsPerRound}} programs back in order. Partly right still scores. You have {{duration}} seconds.

bugs.name: Bug hunt
bugs.rules: Find the line that holds the mistake in {{questionsPerRound}} programs. The faster you find it, the more points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

ask.linearResult: Which index does the linear search return? (-1 when it finds nothing)

typeOf.passed: Yes or no, nothing else — boolean.
typeOf.initial: Exactly one character — char, in single quotes.
typeOf.name: Several characters — String, in double quotes.
typeOf.price: Euros and cents have decimals — double.
typeOf.index: An index is a whole number — int.
typeOf.temperature: A temperature has decimal places — double.
typeOf.letter: A single letter is a char.
typeOf.logged: Logged in or not — that is a boolean.
typeOf.email: An email address is text, so a String.
typeOf.floor: A floor is counted in whole numbers — int.

why.widening: As soon as a double is involved Java keeps the decimals — and prints them with a .0.
why.intDivision: Two whole numbers make an integer division: the remainder is dropped.
why.cast: The (double) in front of the first value turns this into a decimal division.
why.truncate: (int) cuts the decimals off; it does not round.
why.round: Math.round rounds to the nearest whole number.
why.concat: Java works left to right: the number is glued to the text first, then the second one.
why.bracketed: The bracket is computed first and only then glued to the text.
why.zeroIndex: Counting starts at 0: charAt(0) is the first character.
why.length: length() counts every character; the last index is length() - 1.
why.substring: substring(a, b) stops before position b.
why.equals: Strings are compared with equals, never with ==

bugs.semicolon: Every statement ends with a semicolon.
bugs.paren: The bracket around the condition is never closed.
bugs.assign: A condition compares with ==; a single = assigns.
bugs.comma: Java writes the decimal separator as a point, not a comma.
bugs.charQuotes: A char goes in single quotes; double quotes make it a String.
bugs.boolean: The truth values are true and false, written in lower case.
bugs.case: Java is case sensitive — the method is called println.
bugs.name: An identifier cannot contain a space.
bugs.parseInt: IO.readln hands back a String; a number needs Integer.parseInt around it.
bugs.emptyIf: The semicolon after the condition ends the branch — the block always runs.
bugs.endless: The counter moves away from the stopping point — the loop never ends.
bugs.offByOne: The loop runs one step too far; the valid head is i < array.length.
bugs.index: Counting starts at 0: the last valid index is length - 1.
bugs.equals: Strings are compared with equals; == compares the references.
bugs.intDivision: Both values are int, so this divides as whole numbers — the average is wrong.
bugs.concat: The plus glues to a text here instead of adding; the sum belongs in brackets.
bugs.shadow: An inner block cannot declare a variable that already exists outside — the second int is one too many.
bugs.noReturn: The value is computed but never handed back — return is missing.
bugs.forCommas: The three parts of a for head are separated by semicolons, not by commas.
bugs.stringQuotes: A String goes in double quotes; single ones are for a single character.
bugs.intDecimal: The right-hand side is a decimal — an int holds whole numbers only.
bugs.typeMismatch: The quotes turn the number into text, and there is no arithmetic on text.
bugs.charMulti: A char holds exactly one character, not two.
bugs.undeclared: That name is never declared — only what has been declared may be used.
bugs.elseCondition: else takes no condition; else if is the one that does.
bugs.arrayNew: An array is created with square brackets, not round ones.
bugs.elseIfOrder: The second branch can never run — anything meeting its condition was caught by the first.
bugs.counterReset: The sum is set back to 0 on every pass, so only the last value is left.
bugs.offByOneStart: Counting starts at 0 — starting at 1 leaves the first value of the array unread.
bugs.maxInitZero: Every value is negative; with 0 as the starting value the starting value wins, not the array.
bugs.alwaysTrue: With || the condition is always true — && is what was meant.
bugs.swapNoTemp: This assignment overwrites erste before the old value is saved; a swap needs a helper variable.

output.name: Java as a calculator
output.rules: Predict the output of {{questionsPerRound}} short programs. Watch out for / and %: two whole numbers make an integer division. The calculator at the bottom is yours to use — but it answers 7 / 2 with 3.5, and Java prints 3. You have {{duration}} seconds.

types.name: Data types
types.summary: int or double, char or String — and what the plus does
types.rules: Decide for {{questionsPerRound}} tasks which output appears or which type fits. 9 and 9.0 are two different answers. You have {{duration}} seconds.

variables.name: Follow the variable
variables.summary: Which value is in the variable at the end?
variables.rules: Follow what ends up in the variables of {{questionsPerRound}} programs. The = does not mean “is equal to” but “gets the value”. You have {{duration}} seconds.

logic.name: Logic duel
logic.summary: true or false — &&, || and ! against the clock
logic.rules: Decide for {{questionsPerRound}} expressions whether they are true or false. Mind the order: ! before && before ||. The faster you are right, the more points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

branch.name: Branches
branch.rules: Decide for {{questionsPerRound}} programs which output appears. Java checks from top to bottom and takes the first branch that fits. You have {{duration}} seconds.

loops.name: Loops
loops.rules: Read {{questionsPerRound}} loops: sometimes you count the passes, sometimes you write down every value printed, in order. Watch whether the condition sits in the head or in the foot. You have {{duration}} seconds.

robot.name: Robot
robot.summary: Follow the program and say where the robot stops
robot.rules: Follow {{questionsPerRound}} programs and tap the square the robot comes to rest on. vor() moves it one square, links() and rechts() turn it where it stands. Nothing here has to be worked out. You have {{duration}} seconds.

trail.name: Trail
trail.summary: Spot which route the program drives
trail.rules: For {{questionsPerRound}} programs: which of the four trails does the robot drive? The wrong ones are not random — each comes from one misreading, a turn the other way or a loop run once too often. You have {{duration}} seconds.

parsons.name: Order the Lines
parsons.summary: Rebuild a program from its shuffled lines
parsons.rules: Rebuild {{questionsPerRound}} programs from their lines. Watch the braces — a closing brace says which block has just ended. Every line in the right place counts. You have {{duration}} seconds.

structogram.name: Structograms
structogram.summary: Match a program to its structogram
structogram.rules: Match {{questionsPerRound}} programs to the structogram that says the same thing. Watch which branch goes where, and whether the condition sits at the top or at the bottom. You have {{duration}} seconds.

methods.name: Methods
methods.rules: Predict for {{questionsPerRound}} programs what the call prints. Watch the order of the arguments — and whether the method hands anything back at all. You have {{duration}} seconds.

arrays.name: Arrays
arrays.rules: Answer {{questionsPerRound}} questions about arrays. Remember: counting starts at 0, and length comes without brackets. You have {{duration}} seconds.

sorting.name: Searching and sorting
sorting.rules: Run a method by hand for {{questionsPerRound}} tasks: one pass of bubble sort, one step of selection sort, or the comparisons of a linear search. Write several numbers in order, separated by spaces. You have {{duration}} seconds.

bugs.name: Bug hunt
bugs.rules: Find the line that holds the mistake in {{questionsPerRound}} programs. The faster you find it, the more points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

intuition.title: Gut Feeling
intuition.description: Match colours, name pictures, untangle wires, chase targets — nine stations that need no prior knowledge at all.
intuition.colorPrompt: Match the colour on the left.

color.seam: wanted on the left, your mix on the right

intuition.lampPrompt: Switch lamps on until it adds up to:
intuition.pixelPrompt: What is it? The earlier you tap, the more points.
intuition.dialPrompt: Turn the ring until there are words.
intuition.untanglePrompt: Drag the dots until no wire crosses another.
intuition.routePrompt: Tap your way from the green dot to the red one.
intuition.swapPrompt: Sort the cards — you may only ever swap two that are side by side.
intuition.swapPar_one: one move would have done it

farbe.name: Match the colour
farbe.summary: Three sliders until the colour fits
farbe.rules: A colour on the left, yours on the right. Move the three sliders until you cannot see the seam any more — close counts too. {{questionsPerRound}} colours in {{duration}} seconds.

lampen.name: Lamps
lampen.summary: Switch lamps on until the number fits
lampen.rules: Every lamp is worth a number. Switch on as many as it takes to add up to exactly the number asked for. {{questionsPerRound}} numbers in {{duration}} seconds.

pixel.name: What is it?
pixel.summary: Name it while it is still a blur
pixel.rules: The picture slowly sharpens. The earlier you know what it is, the more points — but a wrong guess scores nothing. {{questionsPerRound}} pictures in {{duration}} seconds.

drehen.name: Turn the ring
drehen.summary: Turn until the jumble becomes words
drehen.rules: There is a German sentence hidden in the jumble of letters. Turn the ring until you can read it. {{questionsPerRound}} sentences in {{duration}} seconds.

kabel.name: Tangled wires
kabel.summary: Drag the dots until nothing crosses
kabel.rules: Drag the dots until no wire crosses another. It always works out — and every wire you pull free counts, even if you do not finish. {{questionsPerRound}} tangles in {{duration}} seconds.

weg.name: Which way?
weg.summary: The quickest route across the map
weg.rules: Every road says how long it takes. Tap your way from the green dot to the red one — the quickest way is rarely the one that looks shortest. {{questionsPerRound}} maps in {{duration}} seconds.

nachbarn.name: Neighbours only
nachbarn.summary: Sort in as few moves as you can
nachbarn.rules: Put the cards in order by size. But you may only ever swap two that lie next to each other — and the fewer moves, the more points. {{questionsPerRound}} rows in {{duration}} seconds.

ziele.name: Target practice
ziele.summary: Hit the targets before they shrink
ziele.rules: Targets appear and shrink while they are there. Tap them while they are still big — the earlier, the more points. The run lasts {{duration}} seconds.

ampel.name: Traffic light
ampel.rules: The panel is red. The moment it turns green, tap as fast as you can. Tap too early and that light is lost. {{duration}} seconds, and as many lights as fit.

intuition.targetPrompt: Hit the targets before they are gone.
intuition.lightPrompt: Wait for green — then as fast as you can.

flow.rules: Work through the assessment on your own device, at your own pace. It is marked as you go, right here on your device. Your teacher sees how far you are and how it went — never what you wrote — and nobody else in the class sees anything about you.
